case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: S.C. v. New Jersey Department of Children and Families
key_cases.holding: The Court upheld the Department's 'not established' investigative category but required improved notice, a credible-evidence basis, and an informal opportunity to respond, while rejecting any right to a contested OAL hearing.
key_cases.relevance: S.C. arises from an investigation of alleged corporal punishment reported through school and child-protection channels.
key_cases.quote: We reject that due process considerations require the Department to conduct an adjudicative contested case proceeding either internally or at the Office of Administrative Law for a "not established" finding.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that coercive or suggestive interview techniques can so taint a child's statements that a pretrial hearing on reliability is required before the child's statements or testimony may be admitted.
key_cases.relevance: Michaels arose from disclosures in a day-care setting and shows how adult questioning can shape a child's report.
key_cases.quote: If a child's recollection of events has been molded by an interrogation, that influence undermines the reliability of the child's responses as an accurate recollection of actual events.

key_cases.case_name: In re Allegations of Physical Abuse at Blackacre Academy
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court upheld the Institutional Abuse Investigation Unit's substantiated finding, holding the unit could report its results to the Department of Education and the affected parents and was not required to hold a hearing first.
key_cases.relevance: Blackacre governs investigations of abuse allegations against staff in school and institutional settings.
key_cases.quote: the IAIU was not required to conduct a formal or informal hearing before placing appellants' names in the Central Registry

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. P.W.R.
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the abuse-or-neglect finding, holding the record inadequate to establish a Title 9 violation and that an occasional slap to a teenager's face as discipline, causing no bruising or marks, is not 'excessive corporal punishment' under N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.21(c)(4)(b).
key_cases.relevance: P.W.R. arose from a report routed through school and family channels about slapping and is the substantive standard governing such school-sourced discipline referrals.
key_cases.quote: Limiting state involvement only to interference with excessive corporal punishment requires the exercise of judgment by reviewing courts before a finding of physical abuse is entered against a parent.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. A.R.G.
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed as modified and remanded for de novo reconsideration, holding that 'aggravated circumstances' excusing the Division from reasonable reunification efforts under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-11.3 is a fact-specific inquiry and that a parent must first receive notice of the underlying facts and theory the State will rely on.
key_cases.relevance: A.R.G. begins with an anonymous call to a school nurse who verified the child's bruises and reported to DYFS, illustrating the school-based intake pathway.
key_cases.quote: Moreover, any circumstances that increase the severity of the abuse or neglect, or add to its injurious consequences, equates to "aggravated circumstances."

search_keywords: New Jersey Department of Children and Families

state_agency.name: New Jersey Division of Child Protection and Permanency

reporting_details: New Jersey is a universal-reporter state: any person having reasonable cause to believe that a child has been subjected to child abuse must report it immediately to the Division of Child Protection and Permanency through the 24-hour State Central Registry hotline, 1-877-652-2873 (1-877 NJ ABUSE), and may do so anonymously, and any person who fails to report is a disorderly person (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.10; N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.14).

other: Continued inappropriate placement of a child in an institution with the knowledge that the placement has resulted and may continue to result in harm to the child's mental or physical well-being

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediate (by the end of the work day) or within 24 hours for a child protective services report; within 72 hours or 5 work days for a child welfare service referral
timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry accepts the report and assigns it to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: When contact cannot be made within the assigned timeframe the worker must make and document a good faith effort (CP&P-II-C-2-300(G); CP&P-II-C-5-125).

timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry assigns the CPS report to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Good cause must be established and an extension approved by the local office manager or designee before day 60 (CP&P-II-C-6-200).
